Right, let me run through this quickly because I have another call at half past. We are looking at forty-eight employees, not the forty-two on the old spreadsheet, and we want to be live on the first of March. Ralph at head office signs off on the budget, so nothing moves until he has seen it, and he is in London, which means we lose the afternoon every time we need him. What I need from you is the employee file by the tenth. Not the twentieth, the tenth, because we lose a week at the other end if it slips. Anything you cannot answer today, just note it down and come back to me by email.

I am sending you this before you read the minutes, because the minutes are wrong. There were six of us on that call and at least two people talking over each other the whole time. David said the tenth. Then somebody else, and I still do not know who it was, said the twentieth, and nobody corrected it. A fourth person joined halfway through, asked two questions about the payroll numbers, and never said his name. I did not want to interrupt, so I did not, and now we have a document that says the twentieth and a client who thinks it says the tenth. Next time, please, just stop me and ask.
